noise.name: Noise: Fields and Possible Bodies
noise.truth: A field can be read as colour, relief, an address or a threshold. Each use makes different bodies and passages possible.
noise.qfep_connection: The QFEP vocabulary invites us to ask how variation is weighted and what a chosen representation makes possible or withholds. These halls do not calculate QFE, equate spatial coherence with memory, or measure political freedom through noise.
noise.formula: Layered example: f(p) = Σᵢ aᵢ n(fᵢ p). Receiving operations turn sampled values into colour, displacement, warped addresses or occupancy.
noise.description: Follow a value from a column to a surface, from a threshold into an occupied volume, and from a borrowed address into a room you can enter. Hold a field steady while changing what receives it. Walk its ground, return with another body, and compare Perlin with OpenSimplex2 under shared conditions. Noise can lend an object an organic gesture; its ease can also let a familiar blob arrive before a different form has been imagined. The main spine continues to Cellular Automata, where stored states and neighbours take on another role. Lab Path remains an optional return.
learning_objectives: Distinguish spatial relationships, repeated sampling and stored state
Follow one field through colour, relief and thresholded occupancy
Compare layered contributions and the mappings that display their sum
Use a coordinate field to change where another field is sampled
Relate a sampled surface to collision, route and body scale
Compare Perlin and OpenSimplex2 without confusing the display grid with either generator
Investigate the pleasure and limits of noise as an easy organic gesture

artifact_groups.rationale: From enforced coordinates and initial spacing to independent image/audio constructions, then temporal relationships embodied as moving views.
Three column drivers enter one form; a separately pulsing orb and its six-part relative extend the comparison to appearance, independent time and construction.
One field received as relief or colour; a basin isolates and combines retained terrain contributions.
The same threshold decisions at model and body scale; occupied connectivity does not guarantee a usable route.
A layered sum dresses an enclosure; colour, apparent depth and collision can answer differently.
Domain warping borrows another address; values shape an enclosing surface while its floor and doors stay pinned.
A fixed terrain meets proposed routes, recorded walks and reversible changes of visitor scale.
Matched fields and walk-through arches expose which conditions change; the organic shortcut leads into Cellular Automata.
Optional grid-lane reflection outside the museum spine; the main Perlin/Simplex ending carries its invitation to return.
